synopsis.heading: The core rule
synopsis.body: A singular subject takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb. The hard part is finding the real subject, which is often separated from its verb by a phrase.

synopsis.heading: Ignore the phrase in between
synopsis.body: Words like along with, as well as, together with and in addition to do not change the subject. The captain, along with his players, was invited.

synopsis.heading: Either/or and neither/nor
synopsis.body: The verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. Neither the teacher nor the students were present. Neither the students nor the teacher was present.

tricks.title: Cover the middle
tricks.body: Put your finger over everything between the subject and the verb, including prepositional phrases. Read what is left; the error usually jumps out.
tricks.example: The box of chocolates [are] on the table → The box is

tricks.title: Watch "one of the"
tricks.body: "One of the + plural noun" takes a singular verb because the subject is "one". But "one of those who" takes a plural verb because "who" refers to the plural noun.
tricks.example: One of the boys is absent. He is one of those who work hard.

tricks.title: Amounts are singular
tricks.body: Sums of money, distances and periods of time treated as one amount take a singular verb.
tricks.example: Ten kilometres is a long walk.
